clue.text: Old-fashioned type given repeated encouragement to act

indicators.note: repeated tells us the short word of encouragement is written twice in a row

parts.note: 'Do!' or 'Go on, do it' urges someone to act

explanation.surface: A stuffy traditionalist keeps being urged to get on and do something.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct bird gives the idiom for a person hopelessly behind the times, an old fogey.

clue.text: Observe legal process that keeps paper money secure

parts.note: to observe something is to note it
a case is an action or suit brought in a court of law

explanation.surface: Watch the legal procedure meant to safeguard banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet for banknotes, so its job is holding paper currency safely.

clue.text: Secret old Conservative sect

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
a sect is a small religious group, a cult

explanation.surface: A clandestine group of elderly Tories forming a hidden sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: occult knowledge is hidden, esoteric, kept from the uninitiated.

clue.text: Arrived, carrying round university emblem, in disguise

indicators.note: carrying means the word for arrived holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: arrived means came
O is round in shape
a flag is an emblem of a nation or group

explanation.surface: Someone turned up in disguise, bearing a university crest around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: camouflage is concealment by disguise, as of soldiers or vehicles.

clue.text: Put down at destination, fall asleep

definitions.meaning: to set a passenger down where they are going

explanation.surface: A taxi passenger is dropped off and promptly nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the phrasal verb: deliver someone to a place, and drift into sleep.

clue.text: Gloomy person at surgery perhaps needing attention

parts.note: a doctor, DR, works at a surgery, the British word for a GP's practice
to give someone an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A miserable patient at the doctor's needs some care.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a surgery is a doctor's consulting rooms, not just an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drear is a literary word for dismal, cheerless, bleak.

clue.text: Men in leadership roles could make Theresa gruff, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy, used as a verb of imagining, suggests the letters can be reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: Male leaders might turn Theresa grumpy, I suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I suppose', but fancy signals the anagram and I is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: figures looked up to as paternal leaders or mentors.

clue.text: Church faces a very big state of confusion

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very big

explanation.surface: A church confronts an enormous mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: chaos is total disorder and confusion.

clue.text: Discharge — it goes into sort of waterfall

indicators.note: goes into tells us the word it is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a spout is a jet or column of falling water

explanation.surface: A discharge that flows into a type of cascade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to eject from the mouth is to discharge.

clue.text: Recall being all right, always being retrospective about it

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the reversed word surrounds the other piece
retrospective means looking back, so the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always
OK means all right

explanation.surface: To recall something is fine, as long as you're forever looking back on it.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER read backwards gives REVE, which goes about OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recall a decree or law is to cancel or withdraw it.

clue.text: Like some Europeans needing boost, with EU taking time to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene means to come between, so these letters go inside the word for boost

parts.note: a tonic is something that gives a boost

explanation.surface: Europeans need a lift, with the EU taking its time to step in.
explanation.definitionFit: Teutonic describes Germanic peoples, a group within Europe.

clue.text: Iron Man engaging a publicist

indicators.note: engaging here means taking on, so the word for man takes the a in front of it

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: The superhero Iron Man hires a PR person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Man' looks like the superhero; it splits into iron and man.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a press agent handles publicity for a client.

clue.text: Boy and friend going under water at a certain time of the year

definitions.text: at a certain time of the year

indicators.note: in a down entry, going under puts these pieces below the word for water

parts.note: the sea is water
a son is a boy
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A boy and his friend sink beneath the waves at some point in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done seasonally happens during a particular season.

clue.text: Wild animal about to run

indicators.note: about signals a turn around, so the word for the animal is read backwards

parts.note: a wolf is a wild animal

explanation.surface: A wild beast is about to bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to run' reads as 'on the point of running'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liquids run or stream; to flow is to run.

clue.text: Very modern country frequently requiring courage

parts.note: a state is a country
oft is an old word for often
heart means courage

explanation.surface: A modern nation often demands bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the latest, most advanced in technology or design.

clue.text: Official in street on eastern part of city?

parts.note: a ward is an electoral division of a city

explanation.surface: A functionary on a street in the east end of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a steward is an official who manages events or a household.

clue.text: Provider of accommodation has house on row for the Spanish to occupy

indicators.note: to occupy means to live inside, so the Spanish article goes inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A landlord with a house on a terrace lets Spaniards move in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel keeper provides lodging for guests.

clue.text: Not all stifled emotions, making protest

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pent-up feelings, only partly suppressed, spill into protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a public demonstration, a march making a protest; 'making' is part of the definition.

clue.text: Report of location attracting wise people and tourists?

indicators.note: report of means the word for location is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a site is a location
seers are prophets, wise people

explanation.surface: News of a place draws in sages and holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists visit famous attractions; the question mark notes they are an example.

clue.text: Holy army isn't bad for holy people

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian church organised like an army

indicators.note: bad means the letters of the word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A religious army that is not wicked, standing in for the devout.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are people recognised for exceptional holiness.

clue.text: Sticky stuff in fire, sinking

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the next words, running across them

explanation.surface: Something gummy in a blaze, going down.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the gummy sap from trees, a sticky substance.

clue.text: A vile drunk getting into vehicle is discourteous

indicators.note: getting into means the shuffled letters go inside the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: An awful drunk climbing into a car is rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges AVILE to VALIE, which goes into CA-R.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and disdainful, showing lack of courtesy.

clue.text: See our lot by street most debased

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
we means our group, us

explanation.surface: Look at our crowd down the road, so degraded.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of low in the sense base or vile, matching most debased.

clue.text: Witty folk who watch their partners at matches?

definitions.meaning: jokers, people known for their wit

definitions.text: who watch their partners at matches?
definitions.meaning: the wives and girlfriends of footballers, famous for attending games

explanation.surface: Jokers who sit in the stands watching their other halves play.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is British tabloid shorthand for the wives and girlfriends of England footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: jokers or wits, and the acronym for footballers' wives and girlfriends.

clue.text: Trotter starts to flog this pottery

parts.note: Del Boy Trotter is the market trader in the British TV comedy Only Fools and Horses

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A wheeler-dealer begins hawking this china.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy, a dodgy market trader in a classic British sitcom, would certainly try to flog pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware from the Dutch town of that name.

clue.text: Seen in tabloid, gent waving weapon

indicators.note: seen in means the shuffled letters appear inside the newspaper name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: waving suggests letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A tabloid photo shows a man brandishing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' shuffles the man's letters; the weapon was a British submachine gun, and The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sten is a British submachine gun of the Second World War.
